We first need to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder parts, which we can do using synthetic division.

We draw up a synthetic division table:

$$
\begin{aligned} & {x}^{2} & {x}^{1} & {x}^{0} \\ -5 & 1 & 7 & 10 \\  & ↓ & -5 & -10 \\  & 1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}
$$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+7x+10}{x+5}=x+2.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{{x}^{2}+7x+10}{x+5}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(x+2)\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x\,\text{d}x+2{\int }_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}{|}_{0}^{1}+2x{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =[\frac{{1}^{2}}{2}-\frac{{0}^{2}}{2}]+2[1-0] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}+2 \\  & =\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
